title: Real benchmark demo. Deceptive edit.
summary: 100x speedup claim reveals an omitted memory spike and crash.
narration: Watch this developer demo. The edited clip claims a 100x performance breakthrough. But when you align it with the original recording, you instantly see what was cut: seconds 5 to 10, where the benchmark memory spiked and threw an out-of-memory error.

title: Deterministic alignment first.
summary: Never let foundation models assert ungrounded omissions.
narration: Misleading edits of developer tutorials, benchmark demos, and product claims cut out critical qualifications. But you cannot simply ask a foundation model to guess what was cut—models hallucinate omissions that never existed. CONTEXT enforces a strict non-negotiable rule: deterministic alignment first. If our acoustic and visual aligner finds no correspondence, the output is 'no material omission'. The Meta model is only permitted to reason over verified, grounded intervals.

title: Live timeline & bounded review.
summary: Synchronized dual-player with bounded Meta Muse Spark review.
narration: Here's a live run. The aligner chunks the media, downsamples 4Hz visual feature grids, and runs normalized acoustic cross-correlation. Within seconds, it locks the correspondence with sub-second accuracy. Notice our dual player: scrubbing the edited video synchronously drives the source. When we click the omission card, it reveals the excised footage. Meta Muse Spark 1.2 explains the exact semantic consequence, bounded strictly by our citation checker: any explanation citing timestamps outside the evidence is rejected.

title: SAM 3.1 detects cropped disclaimers.
summary: Multi-scale spatial tracking isolates peripheral omissions.
narration: Deceptive cuts aren't just temporal—they're spatial. When a widescreen tutorial is reframed or cropped for mobile, key disclaimers and benchmark sidebars vanish. Having passed our SAM 3.1 gate with over 99% pixel recall, CONTEXT runs multi-scale spatial alignment and uses SAM 3.1 to segment and shade the exact peripheral elements cut out of frame.

title: 100% recall. Zero false alarms.
summary: 30 automated FFmpeg edits with 18 benign controls.
narration: Every claim here is backed by reproducible numbers. Before writing a line of tuning code, we froze a labeled eval contract: 30 automated FFmpeg edits, including 18 benign controls—intro trims, 1.25x speed-ups, subtitles, re-encodes, and reorders. Our thresholds were fixed beforehand: at least 80% recall and under 10% false alarms. CONTEXT scored 100% interval recall, 0.0 seconds mean boundary error, and exactly zero false alarms on benign edits.

title: Open source and fully reproducible.
summary: Muse Spark 1.2, SAM 3.1, Docker one-command run.
narration: Here's what each Meta model did: Muse Spark 1.2 provided bounded semantic interpretation; SAM 3.1 powered spatial reframe segmentation. And here is our honest failure case: when an edit undergoes aggressive non-linear speed changes or extreme jump-cuts, the aligner safely abstains rather than making a false accusation. CONTEXT is reproducible with one Docker command. Code, benchmarks, and data are public in our repository.
